newsitem.title: USA: Starcraft names president, restructures unit.
newsitem.headline: Starcraft names president, restructures unit.

text.p: Starcraft Corp said Friday it had named a new president and was implementing a restructuring of its Imperial manufacturing operation in Elkhart, Ind., which will result in the loss of some jobs and a charge to fourth quarter earnings.
Starcraft said it had appointed Michael Schoeffler as president and chief operating officer. He continues as chief financial officer.
Schoeffler succeeds Kelly Rose as president. The post of chief operating officer had been vacant. Rose remains chairman. The changes are effective immediately.
The company makes second-stage van and truck conversions at its Starcraft, Imperial and Lonestar divisions.
Starcraft said its Imperial operation in Elkhart, Ind., will be consolidated into its expanded, 650,000-square-foot manufacturing complex in Goshen, Ind., on December 2.
This is designed to reduce costs and product development time while enhancing operating efficiency and flexibility, Starcraft said.
It said some manufacturing jobs will be eliminated but it declined to give a number.
Imperial will continue to maintain separate sales and marketing departments independent of the Starcraft Automotive Group.
Starcraft said the restructuring will result in a charge to earnings -- in an amount not yet determined -- in the fiscal fourth quarter.

"This consolidation plan dramatically improves our competitiveness. In addition to the reduction in overhead costs, this strategy will allow us to synergize existing engineering, production, computer operations, customer and service support systems," Schoeffler said in a statement.
Shares of Starcraft were trading off 1/8 to 4-3/4.
